title: Rumpelstiltskin (Rumpelstilzchen)
summary: A boastful miller told the king: "I have a daughter who can spin straw into pure gold!"...
full_text:
A boastful miller told the king: "I have a daughter who can spin straw into pure gold!"

The greedy king commanded the maiden to court, locked her in a chamber filled with straw, and ordered: "Spin this straw into gold before dawn, or you shall die!"

The poor miller's daughter wept in despair. Suddenly, a tiny little manikin stepped through the door: "What will you give me if I spin it for you?"

She gave him her necklace, and the imp sat at the wheel: whir, whir, whir! By sunrise, the room was filled with golden bobbins.

The king was thrilled, but his greed was boundless. The next night, he locked her in a larger room; she gave the little man her ring, and again the straw became gold.

On the third night, in an enormous hall of straw, the maiden had nothing left to give. The little man demanded: "Promise me your first-born child when you become queen!" Having no other choice to save her life, she promised.

The king married the miller's daughter. A year later, the young queen gave birth to a beautiful infant, having forgotten the imp.

Suddenly, the little man stepped into her bedchamber: "Now give me what you promised!"

The queen wept, offering all the treasures of the realm to keep her child. Moved by her tears, the manikin said: "I will give you three days; if you can discover my true name, you may keep your child!"

The queen sent messengers across the world to collect every name under heaven. On the first night, she guessed: "Caspar, Melchior, Balthazar!" On the second night: "Ribs-of-Beef, Sheepshanks, Spindleshanks!" But to each, the imp laughed: "That is not my name!"

On the third evening, a messenger returned from the deep forest: "High on a mountain where the fox and hare bid goodnight, I saw a fire burning; and around the fire hopped a comical little man on one leg, singing:
'Today I brew, tomorrow I bake,
Next day the queen's fair child I take;
For little does anyone know my fame,
That Rumpelstiltskin is my name!'"

When the little man arrived at dawn, demanding: "What is my name, Queen?", she asked calmly:
"Is your name Conrad?" "No!"
"Is your name Harry?" "No!"
"Can your name perhaps be... Rumpelstiltskin?"

"The devil told you that! The devil told you that!" shrieked the little man in a fury. He stamped his right foot so deep into the earth that his leg sank in up to his waist; then in his rage, he seized his left foot with both hands and tore himself in two!

The queen embraced her child in peace, freed forever from the shadow of the greedy imp.
moral: Boasting traps us in impossible debts; steadfast maternal love unmasks deceit.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Rumpelstiltskin (Rumpelstilzchen)"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
